security_audit.summary: The skill legitimately requires a Linear API key and documents Bun commands that create and update live Linear issues. Most Markdown backtick detections are false positives, but credential handling, hidden .env usage, and write-capable external commands are confirmed risks that require clear safeguards.

remediation.suggestion: Document least-privilege API key use, avoid showing secrets in prompts, and recommend rotating keys after accidental disclosure.
Warn users to keep .env out of version control and prefer a managed secret store when running shared automation.

remediation.issue: Write operations against live Linear data
remediation.suggestion: Require the assistant to summarize intended create or update actions and get explicit user confirmation before running commands.

remediation.issue: Markdown command examples trigger static command findings
remediation.suggestion: Separate executable examples from option reference text and include safety notes for commands that modify issue records.

content.value_statement: Linear issue work often requires switching from the assistant to the browser. This skill provides CLI guidance for creating and updating Linear issues with common fields.
actual_capabilities: Creates Linear issues with a title and team name.
Updates existing Linear issues by issue identifier or UUID.
Supports descriptions, assignees, priorities, labels, projects, and statuses.
Resolves team, user, and label names case-insensitively.
Can return machine-readable output when the JSON flag is used.
limitations: Requires the Bun runtime to be installed.
Requires a valid LINEAR_API_KEY with suitable workspace permissions.
The scanned package documents command usage but does not include implementation files.
Commands can modify live Linear data and should be confirmed before execution.

use_cases.title: Create Engineering Work Items
use_cases.description: Open new Linear issues with titles, descriptions, labels, projects, and priorities from an assistant conversation.

use_cases.title: Update Delivery Status
use_cases.description: Move existing issues to the correct status and adjust priority or project fields during planning.

use_cases.title: Route Support Follow-Up
use_cases.description: Assign issues, add labels, and clarify descriptions after customer reports become engineering tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Linear issue titled "Fix login error" for the Engineering team. Use medium priority and include a short description from this conversation.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Issue With Metadata
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Linear issue for the Engineering team with the Bug and Urgent labels, high priority, and the assignee named in this thread.

prompt_templates.title: Update an Existing Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Update issue ENG-123 to In Progress, assign it to the requested teammate, and add the Bug label without removing existing labels.

prompt_templates.title: Review and Apply Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare the Linear create or update command for these requested changes. Summarize the target issue, fields, and impact before running it.

output_examples.input: Create a high-priority bug for the Engineering team about failed password reset emails.
output_examples.output: A Linear issue is created for Engineering with high priority, a Bug label, and a concise description of the password reset failure.

output_examples.input: Update ENG-123 to Done and remove its assignee.
output_examples.output: Issue ENG-123 is updated to Done, and the assignee field is cleared after confirmation.

output_examples.input: Add Bug and Urgent labels to ENG-456 without changing other labels.
output_examples.output: Issue ENG-456 keeps its existing labels and receives the additional Bug and Urgent labels.

best_practices: Review the target team, issue ID, assignee, and priority before running write commands.
Use a least-privilege Linear API key and rotate it after accidental exposure.
Use machine-readable output only when another trusted tool needs structured results.
anti_patterns: Do not paste the Linear API key into prompts, issue descriptions, or command arguments.
Do not run bulk updates without checking every issue ID and intended field change.
Do not use broad personal API keys in shared or unattended automation.

faq.question: Does this skill require a Linear API key?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires LINEAR_API_KEY in the environment or a local .env file.

faq.question: Can it create live Linear issues?
faq.answer: Yes. The create command can add new issues to a Linear team.

faq.question: Can it update existing issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It can update title, description, status, assignee, priority, labels, and project fields.

faq.question: Does it support JSON output?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented JSON flag returns machine-readable output for trusted scripting workflows.

faq.question: What runtime does it need?
faq.answer: It needs the Bun runtime installed before the documented commands can run.

faq.question: How should teams use it safely?
faq.answer: Confirm every write action, keep API keys private, and use keys with only the permissions needed.
